Round-6 sealed sets ask about seeds the model never saw, and the prompt carries only the seed number, not the parameters. Apart from seed-independent answers (time grid, step 0 values) and the world's seedless hand-off questions, such questions cannot be answered by rule; expect near-chance scores there. The meaningful round-6 measures are <sim>-heldout.txt (seen records, unseen questions) and the hand-off questions in world-sealed.txt.

The 350,000-token round-6 budget buys only 17 to 20 rollouts per level and 47 worlds (142 rollouts in all). Each rollout keeps all its records but only 32 of its 590 to 1,170 step questions. Learning the dynamics across seeds is not to be expected at this size; --cosmos-tokens scales it (a world costs about 2.7 s, gravity about 2.5 s per rollout here).

Additions beyond the task text, please confirm or drop: (a) <sim>-heldout.txt files (3,040 questions about training seeds that are in no training line; world's is empty); (b) an 'evaluate' command (python -m haishool.round5 evaluate --model ... --lines ...) because the loop's own evaluate knows only the five truth gates; its model path is untested (no torch), only score() with a stand-in model is tested; (c) data/cosmos-v6/prompts.txt; (d) build flags --truth-tokens, --cosmos-tokens, --sealed, --only.

The build uses records() + generate() only, as specified. It does not add substances.facts() (5,624 lines) or reactions.all_facts(): they would not fit the budget. Every table fact is in a record line, but only part of them is also asked as a question (e.g. 1,438 substances fact questions).

Sealed table facts are still in their always-trained record lines (e.g. 'q oxygen valence' is sealed, the oxygen record is trained). For table topics the sealed set therefore measures record-to-answer, and only the calculations measure a rule. Roughly half of the 1,000 sealed draws per table topic are dropped as given away by training (elements 551, reactions 549, forces 542, substances 249, maths 98).

The 'restated question' filter (asked()) is a heuristic: for a check line it takes the shortest start of the claim the gate can answer. It misses reactions 'check ... balanced' against 'balance ...', and elements 'check a heavier_than b' against 'heavier a b' (those checks count as their own question). For forces it uses the gate's meta['inner'].

I edited other agents' modules (allowed by the task, APIs unchanged) to fix two real defects found during integration: gravity and life accepted '1 e 9 9 9 9' as a right answer for any number (cosmos.close(inf, x) was True), and elements, reactions, forces, planets and chem raised OverflowError on a 400-digit answer. Fix: new haishool.truth.is_finite, used in those gates, and close() now returns False for non-finite numbers. The loop test's 'gates at odds' warning is gone.

Leniency left as it is: several simulations accept non-canonical spellings of a right number ('0 0' for 0 in life), and their 5 % / within-1 tolerances accept a wrong last digit. The loop writes the gate's own value back, so training is not affected, only the judged score.

Both rounds are built and the whole suite passes (924 passed, 5 skipped), but nothing has been trained: there is no torch on this machine.

WHAT WAS BUILT
- Round 5 (data/truth-v5): 19,925 training lines, 349,515 tokens of the 350,000 budget, 3,011 sealed questions, 0 lines dropped.
- Round 6 (data/cosmos-v6): 11,750 training lines, 347,481 tokens, 142 training rollouts, 33 sealed rollouts with 1,759 sealed questions, 3,040 held-out questions.
- The build took 3 min 14 s; the world (125 s) and gravity (54 s) are the slow parts, far under the 20-minute limit, so N_train was not reduced.

HOW round5.py WORKS (C:\Users\end\Desktop\Haishool\haishool\round5.py)
- Budget: tokens are counted with haishool.student.tokens plus 1 per line. TRUTH_SHARE = maths 0.30, elements 0.165, substances 0.215, reactions 0.165, forces 0.155. COSMOS_SHARE = nucleo 0.15, gravity 0.17, planets 0.14, chem 0.15, life 0.16, world 0.23.
- Round 5: a topic's n for generate() is fitted to its share (maths 5,099, elements 4,456, substances 3,516, reactions 2,844, forces 3,036). Each topic and purpose has its own SHA-256-derived random generator, so topics do not move each other.
- Round 6: all simulations share one list of training seeds and one of sealed seeds, each taking a prefix. So nucleo seed s is the first hour of world seed s (nucleo's 20 seeds are the first 20 of the world's 47).
- Thinning: per rollout all records are kept, all non-step questions, and 32 step questions drawn by seed; 32 more go to <sim>-heldout.txt.
- Screening: every line is checked before writing. It is dropped and counted if it is over 80 tokens, rejected by its own gate, judged differently by another owning gate, gives a round 1-4 prompt a second answer (84,953 earlier prompts loaded; 0 collisions), or repeats a prompt. A rollout whose conserved() fails is skipped (0 failed).
- Sealed: a sealed question is dropped when any topic's training holds its prompt or a check line that restates it. This was first done per topic; a cross-file check then found 'q helium state' and 'q zinc state' sealed in one topic and trained in the other, so sealed sets are now filtered against all topics' training.
- judge: prints prompt, answer, owner, owners, ok, expected, reason, agree as JSON, over the 5 gates, the 6 simulations and the loop's judge lines. Numbers must be digit tokens ('gravity seed 5 4 4 0 ...'; 'seed 5440' has no owner).
- stats prints both report.json files.

findings.value: q check x minus 1 equals minus 8 x minus 7. a yes.   q check 8 x minus 3 9 equals x minus 3 2 x minus 1. a no.   q check x over 6 equals 1 x 1 6. a no.

All 314 check-x lines put a number directly in front of the separating x; only the convention 'the last x separates' resolves it, the opposite of what '8 x' means everywhere else in the topic. A prompt format cannot be changed cheaply after training.

No common clock: nucleo counts seconds, gravity free-fall times, planets Myr, chem and life steps; the world lines list eras but never an age of the universe, so 'from the start of time' is an order, not a timeline.

No link from rounds 5/6 into the round-4 relation graph (keys were named composition, occurs_in, main_parts to avoid made_of and found_in), so the hops explorer cannot walk from water to hydrogen or from iron to the earth's core.

critic.summary: The build is clean as a file set: a full rebuild in the scratchpad reproduced all 36 data files byte for byte, no line exceeds 80 tokens, no prompt has two answers, yes/no is balanced, sealed and fresh questions hold no unknown token, and the pilot showed the old facts and hops survive such a mix. Against the intent it delivers the closed topics, the gates, the elements, a fair materials table (485 rows) and forces table (31 rows) and a six-level chain, but it falls short in three places: maths is in the memorising regime (5,099 repeated lines, where the repo's own experiment needed a stream of fresh lines to reach 0.93 held-out), the simulations are trained as lookups keyed by seed and step and not as rules (sealed rollouts are unanswerable, 'next' is a record lookup, and the same seed names different universes in the level files and the world), and the feedback of the model's own output has code but not one line of data yet. The main training risks are the 1,600-odd forces and 670 molar-mass/mass-percent calculations that the pilot answered at 0 to 22 % held-out, about 27,500 chaotic 3-digit numbers in rollout records, a 96-token window that cuts a quarter of the rollout tokens off from their seed and step, and a documented train command that names files which do not exist and too few steps. Fix before training, because prompt formats freeze once trained: stream the maths (and other unbounded calc kinds) per pass, add state- or parameter-conditioned simulation questions and gravity params, put every asked metric into a record or stop asking it, separate level seeds from world seeds, replace 'minus 1' by 'never', give check-x a separator word, raise ctx, and correct the train and loop commands plus the loop's sealed-question exclusion. After the first training: run the loop and extend it to the simulations, unify number spelling with rounds 1-4, widen the tables and the maths forms, and fill the chain's gaps (stars, galaxy, organisms, a common clock)."
